blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Stochastic Computer** in *Introduction* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Introduction, § The Stochastic Computer
blocks.md: Repairing the connection-pool race condition requires more than a model call. The system must hold source files and test logs in working and persistent memory, invoke compilers and test runners that read and modify the workspace, supervise which commands may run, and improve future repairs from recorded runs. A classical computer organizes the same requirements, which makes it a convenient map of how the subsystems of an agentic system fit together.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Cost per accepted task matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Under retry-until-accept, C_eff = E[C_attempt]/p_acc, so acceptance divides the whole attempt cost and any mechanism pays for its overhead only if it lowers this ratio.

questions.q: The section **The Stochastic Computer** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Under retry-until-accept, C_eff = E[C_attempt]/p_acc, so acceptance divides the whole attempt cost and any mechanism pays for its overhead only if it lowers this ratio.

Self-report, static analysis, visible tests, sealed tests, and formal verification form a default ordering of acceptance evidence that coverage can override, and every check is a bounded claim narrower than the task.
Constraints never rest on the model: bounds close mechanically below it and acceptance rests on external evidence above it, and greater exposure demands stronger closure.
The characteristic agent failure is well-formed, credible, and wrong, so fail-stop monitors record success and agreement among samples from one model sets no bound on wrong answers.
